text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- From February 1, foreign airlines will collect airport taxes and remit them to federal airport authority, the authority says.
- Cocoa traders in main cocoa growing centre of Nigeria's Ondo state denounce forestry agency taxes as illegal.
- Fifteen illegal miners arrested in central Nigerian state of Niger last year now face prosecution, says state government.
- Shell oil company donates drugs to oil-producing state of Akwa Ibom for victims of flooding last year.
- Foreigners boost Nigeria's capital market by investing $32.96 million in it last year, stock exchange boss says.
- Cabinet will meet in the capital Abuja on Tuesday followed by meeting of ruling military council to finalise this year's fiscal budget, officials say.
- Banks suspend forex dealing pending broadcast of fiscal 1997 budget.
- Government accepts Central Bank's proposal to sell off distressed banks, officials say.
- Customs collects 69.3 billion naira in first 11 months of last year, some 21.9 billion naira more than what it collected in the whole of 1995, says its boss Brigadier-General Sam Ango.
- Newly created Ekiti state says it has received 230 million naira from federal accounts for October-December as its share of national revenue.
- Unnamed foreign banks show interest in investing in Nigeria following new regulations permitting 100 percent ownership of businesses by foreigners, say Central Bank sources.
- Nigeria and seven Islamic nations meet in Istanbul, Turkey, to forge closer economic relations among themselves and to plan for summit of their heads of state later this year.
